D-JCC25.title: Journals of the Continental Congress, 1774–1789, vol. 25 (Library of Congress, 1922), archive.org OCR

episode.outcome: The audience does not end with the handover of the commission. The President reads Congress's answer. It replies to Washington's two requests (care for his confidential officers, and commending the country to God) and closes with a prayer for him. The 24 December entry then moves straight to routine business and records nothing further about the audience.
episode.quote: And for you we address to him our earnest prayers, that a life so beloved may be fostered with all his care; that yoiu- days may be happy as they have been illustrious; and that he wiU finally give you that reward which this world cannot give.

additions.why: The editors' note on the 20 December vote records only that the sense of the House was taken with yeas and nays. It states no result. This gives the 'no result shown' claim (A1/N1) an exact scope.

additions.start: Thia report, in the writing of James McHenry
additions.why: The printed text of Congress's answer is McHenry's draft and still carries revision marks (e.g. 'safety and triumph success'). Readers should know the quoted answer comes from a revised draft. The two passages the piece quotes are not affected by the revisions.

quote.quote: Sense of the Ilouae taken on the competency of seven atatea to receive the resignation of Commander in Cliief, with yeaa and nays, December 20, 1783.

context_issues.problem: The text says 'in the portion of the roll call cited here', implying the roll call is incomplete. The reading range (with U-E21) shows the full member roll call: Forster, Gerry and Osgood also voted ay, and Partridge was the only no. The paragraph should also cite U-E21.

quote.quote: Mf Forster, ay Gerry, ay Osgood, ay

context_issues.problem: Congress's answer is quoted without saying that it is printed from McHenry's draft, which carries revisions and Bankson's bracketed entries. The quoted phrases are clean, but readers should know the source is a draft.

quote.quote: Thia report, in the writing of James McHenry, is in the Papers of the Continental Congress, No. 19, VI, folio 461.

review.overall: The piece already covers the ending (Congress's answer and its point-by-point reply) and has no serious truncation errors. Two fixes are needed: the vote-result claim should state its scope precisely and note the full roll call, and the uncertainty note's 'no private account was available / unknowable' should be narrowed to 'not consulted, so this piece cannot report'.
